findings.obligation: architecture.md line 62 (open-host narrowing in the downstream modules set-up patterns); craftsmanship rule 2: one owner per fact
findings.observation: Design ownership question, not a verdict on behaviour. Mechanically sound: the composite properties keep the declared pattern-roles files unchanged and tests stay strict. But the open-host boundary is now written four ways: ModuleRules.cs SetUpBehindItsContracts negative regex; WorkItemsModuleBoundariesArchUnitTest.cs SetUpOpenToTheContextsBuildingOnIt positive regex Contracts(\.|$); OrganisationSetupIsAnOpenHostArchUnitTest.cs SetUpModule + ".Contracts" list; composite TheNamespacedUpstreamCodeAndSetUpBehindItsContracts and TheForbiddenCodeAndSetUpBehindItsContracts. architecture.md line 62 says S5 narrows the downstream modules' set-up patterns; the diff instead adds properties. Crafter reason in ModuleRules.cs: "A property, not a constant: the namespace-move law reads constants and fields for the types they see".
findings.remediation: Architect decides and records in architecture.md: either keep the composite-property route and name ModuleRules as the single owner, deriving the positive and negative set-up patterns from one constant, or move the narrowing into the declared pattern roles as line 62 states. Behaviour is not in question; ownership is.
